conviction_note: The one hard number is a probable fiscal-Q4 revenue miss: 1,708 BTC mined times monthly mean BTC prices gives about $121M. The same method reproduces fiscal Q3 at $138.3M against $138.0M reported. Consensus is $126-137M. Against that sit a mechanical GAAP/adjusted-EBITDA beat from the +43% BTC rally in the quarter, a 30.6% short interest and a stock already down 39% in 20 days. The skew (+13 vol pts downside paid) and the run-up point opposite ways, so p_up stays near 50 (47) on a widened abs move of 9%. The sum of the findings (-0.7) and the scaled number (-0.54) agree in sign and size.
bar: Revenue, the only line with a computable print. Consensus is disputed across three sources: $126.3M (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CLSK/earnings-forecasts, EPS -$0.37), $130.28M (Yahoo, 13 analysts, https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CLSK/analysis, EPS -$0.37) and $137.22M (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/CLSK/estimates, EPS -$0.26). I sized against roughly $128M, the midpoint of the two sources that roughly agree. The company gives no numeric guidance (Q3 FY26 release, https://finviz.com/news/378886/cleanspark-reports-third-fiscal-quarter-2026-results). Because the bar is disputed, the revenue finding is capped small. For context on what the stock actually trades on, AI/HPC leasing: Sandersville is a signed 20-year $6.6B lease with a Meta unit, RFS in calendar Q4 2027. Texas is 885 MW under exclusivity with the same tenant and has no lease.
positioning_check: Short interest is 78,727,139 shares, 30.65% of shares outstanding, with 4.57 days to cover on 17.2M average daily volume (settlement 2026-10-30, flat versus 10-15; https://altindex.com/ticker/clsk/short-interest). On today's 19.8M 20-day average volume that is about 4 days. Part of it is plausibly convertible-arbitrage hedging: D. E. Shaw filed a 13G/A on 2026-11-16 showing 6.7% at 2026-09-30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/827876/000110465926128322/primary_doc.xml). Skew is +13.12 vol points (25d put IV over 25d call IV), so the market is paying for downside. Put/call open interest is 0.22, call-heavy. Spot is $5.005: -38.9% over 20 days, -18.6% over 5 days, 2.35% above the 52-week low and -73% from the 52-week high. The event-implied move is 5.26% net of ordinary vol, inside an 11.89% 3-day straddle.

findings.finding: Fiscal Q4 (Jul-Sep 2026) revenue should land near $121M. The company's own monthly updates give 586 + 593 + 529 = 1,708 BTC mined, down 11% from 1,925 in fiscal Q3. At July/Aug/Sep mean BTC prices of $63.9k/$69.5k/$80.5k (BGeometrics daily tables) that comes to about $121.3M. The same arithmetic on Apr/May/Jun (640/671/614 BTC at $73.7k/$78.0k/$63.0k) gives $138.3M against $138.0M reported, so the method is calibrated to within 0.2%. Consensus is $126.3M (Benzinga) / $130.3M (Yahoo, 13 analysts) / $137.2M (Chartmill), which puts the miss at about 4-12%. This would be the fourth revenue miss in the last five quarters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue misses have been sold only mildly here. Q3 FY26 missed $142.2M with $138.0M and closed -3.53% close-to-close (baseline; Cointelegraph reported -5.5% on the day). Q4 FY25 missed $227.1M with $223.7M, fell 2.3% after hours, then closed +13.79% on tenant-onboarding commentary. Q1 FY26 missed and fell 19% on the day into a crypto selloff (Decrypt), then closed +21.96% the next session. The stock trades on AI/HPC news more than on mining revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: All three consensus figures sit above what the company's own production times the realised BTC tape implies, and the highest ($137M) is nearly the fiscal-Q3 level despite 11% fewer coins. If the market had priced a $121M quarter, the published estimates would have been revised to about $120M. They have not.
findings.independence: Uses three company documents: the July/August figures via The Block (https://www.theblock.co/news/markets/2026-09-14-bitcoin-production-rebounds-august-bitfufu-edges-higher-cleanspark-canaan-slips-414660), the September update (above) and the Q3 release for calibration (https://finviz.com/news/378886/cleanspark-reports-third-fiscal-quarter-2026-results). Prices come from BGeometrics (https://bgeometrics.com/reports/monthly/2026-09.html, plus the -07 and -08 pages). This is one computation, so independence is none beyond the calibration check.

findings.finding: GAAP EPS and adjusted EBITDA should print far above consensus on a mechanical bitcoin fair-value gain. BTC rose from about $58.6k on 2026-06-30 to $83.6k on 2026-09-30 (+42.7%). CleanSpark held 13,924 BTC at June 30 and 13,530 at Sept 30, which implies roughly a $300M+ pre-tax fair-value gain before covered-call losses (1,200 BTC were called away in Aug-Sep at below-market strikes). Fiscal Q3 ex-fair-value was about -$107M. Net income is therefore likely positive, on the order of +$0.4 to +$1.0 per share, against a -$0.37/-$0.26 consensus. The company's adjusted EBITDA includes the fair-value line (Q3 was -$113M on a -$116M fair-value loss), so it should also flip strongly positive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has looked through fair-value swings. Q1 FY26 posted a $378.7M net loss mostly from BTC marks and closed +21.96% the next session. Q4 FY25's year-end gain was wiped out by noncash tax adjustments (net loss $0.9M), and the stock still closed +13.79%. The EPS headline has not set direction.
findings.why_not_priced: Both published EPS consensus figures are negative, so the aggregators carry no mark-to-market gain. A headline 'EPS beat' is likely and could move the after-hours tape. Holders know BTC has since fallen to about $61k, which implies a fiscal-Q1 FY27 reversal of most of this gain, so the line is largely discounted. It is a remeasurement with no path to the guide, hence the small size.
findings.independence: Holdings come from the June update (https://blockspace.media/insight/cleanspark-bitcoin-production-holdings-june-2026/) and the September update. The Q3 FV loss and adjusted EBITDA treatment come from the Q3 release (https://finviz.com/news/378886/cleanspark-reports-third-fiscal-quarter-2026-results). A risk to the sign: year-end tax adjustments erased the gain in Q4 FY25 (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/cleanspark-stock-dips-after-hours-on-q4-revenue-miss/cL53OM3REgV).

findings.finding: Mining economics deteriorated through the quarter and after it, and the company stopped monthly reporting. September average operating hashrate was 36.0 EH/s against 50 EH/s nameplate, down from 42.6 in June and 38.3 in August, and only 808 MW of 1.8 GW contracted power was in use. Since 2026-09-30, BTC has fallen from $83.6k to about $61.1k (Fortune, 2026-11-23, -25% in a month). The October-November production, uptime and any miner retirement or impairment will appear for the first time in this release or on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no guidance history. The company gives no numeric guide, and management declined in August to forecast mining economics ('I don't know what the future holds 24 months from now', Q3 call). Mining-line disappointments have produced single-digit moves (Q3 FY26: -3.53%).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is -39% in 20 days, so BTC weakness is known. The unseen part is company-level: production and uptime for two months with no public data, plus any decision to retire or impair ASICs at a $61k hashprice. If that were priced, the 3,475 BTC posted as derivative collateral and the $400M BTC-backed credit lines would already be discussed in the wire copy. I found no such discussion.
findings.independence: Hashrate and holdings come from the company's September update (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/cleanspark-still-has-13-k-bitcoin-on-its-books-but-ending-monthly-updates/cZD6qGtRBn2). Credit lines and treasury stance come from the Q3 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15734682484630528). This is macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: Texas is the line the stock has traded on since 2026-11-04, and this call is management's first scheduled comment since the election. CLSK fell 11% and then 17% on Nov 4-5 after Gina Hinojosa, who backs a data-center permit moratorium, won the governor's race. KBW downgraded to Market Perform with a $9.50 target, and Bernstein cut its target to $11 from $24. The Sandersville tenant (a Meta unit) holds exclusivity over up to 885 MW at Sealy and Brazoria with no lease signed and no disclosed expiry. Sandersville itself is outside ERCOT, fully funded by $2.276B of 7.875% notes, and on track for RFS in calendar Q4 2027. Any statement on the Texas exclusivity (a lease, an extension, or a lapse) or a Georgia expansion (the line study for +500 MW at Washington, GA) is a two-sided catalyst.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Nov 2025 the CFO's 'not if but when' tenant comment took a -2.3% after-hours dip to a +13.79% close. The July 2026 Sandersville lease plus Texas exclusivity lifted the stock about 10% (Blockspace).
findings.why_not_priced: The Texas risk itself is priced: the 26% two-day drop and the target cuts are the visible pricing. What is not priced is the direction of management's answer, which I could not source. There was no 8-K after 2026-09-25 (EDGAR submissions), so nothing new has been disclosed since the election. Sized 0 with a wide band.
findings.independence: Bernstein names CLSK among the miners most exposed to ERCOT approval (https://cointelegraph.com/news/texas-electric-grid-moratorim-btc-miners-bernstein). ERCOT's audit is due mid-December (https://www.tikr.com/blog/cleanspark-lost-21-in-a-week-to-a-new-52-week-low-bernstein-still-sees-62-upside), after the window.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print as a crowded short at a capitulation low. Short interest is 78.7M shares (30.65% of shares outstanding, 4.6 days to cover, 2026-10-30). Spot is $5.005, -38.9% over 20 days and -18.6% over 5, 2.35% above the 52-week low. Market value is about $1.28B on 256.8M shares, against roughly $825M of BTC at $61k (13,530 BTC) plus a signed $6.6B lease. Both of the last two prints that came in after deep pre-print selloffs closed sharply higher (+13.79% Nov 2025, +21.96% Feb 2026).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: From the baseline's seven prints: up 4 of 7, median |move| 6.06%. The two largest were rebounds after heavy pre-print declines (+21.96%, +13.79%). The two most recent were mild declines (-5.8%, -3.53%) without such a pre-print collapse.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew (+13 vol points downside) says the option market is still paying for further downside, so this finding runs against the skew. The reasons to think the skew overstates downside on this print: much of the short is likely hedge inventory (D. E. Shaw 13G/A) that covers as conversion deltas fall, and the -18.6% five-day slide has no company-specific news behind it beyond BTC at $61k. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: D. E. Shaw 13G/A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/827876/000110465926128322/primary_doc.xml). baseline_tension: The revenue miss and the BTC slide agree with the +13 vol-point put skew. The crowded short and the -39% 20-day run-up cut against it. On net I lean slightly negative, at a much smaller size than the skew implies.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (disputed bar: three revenue consensus sources between $126M and $137M): revenue finding cut from -1.5 to -1.2
Rule 2 (one-offs): BTC fair-value EPS beat filed as one_off and cut from +0.8 to +0.4

Rule 7 (crowded short of 30.6%): mining-economics negative cut from -0.8 to -0.6. The positioning positive runs against a +13 skew, so it was cut from +1.0 to +0.7, with the reason the skew may be wrong stated
Untrustworthy-history rule: checked the baseline's dates against confirmed releases (Nov 25 2025, Feb 5 2026, Aug 6 2026 all match quarterly 8-K results), so the history was used as is
